note: Chapter-3 mini-games „Die Fallblatttafel“ (Bahnhof Veltrava, Alexei) and „Die Garderobe“ (Palais, Konrad): UI strings (mg.flap.*, mg.cloak.*) and the two finds (explore.veltrava.station.flap_board.*, explore.veltrava.hall.cloak_tokens.*). Owner: minigames r7 (TECHNICAL_ARCHITECTURE §12.8).

strings.explore.veltrava.station.flap_board.text: The arrivals board had stuck at our train: a carrier pin, three flaps caught together. In Karsk I’d have had a screwdriver for it; here I had time. Now it reads: 8:41, special from Moscow via Karsk, platform 5. The KARSK flap is new, white, not yellowed – the others are older than the agreement. For a year now my town has stood on a board abroad.
strings.mg.flap.title: The split-flap board
strings.mg.flap.subtitle: The arrivals board is stuck on its top line – at the train Alexei came on. The maintenance hatch is only pushed shut.
strings.mg.flap.instruction: Set the line as on the posted timetable. The drums only flip forwards; once everything is right, the line locks in by itself.
strings.mg.flap.instruction_compact: Set the top line – Alexei’s train this morning – as on the posted timetable. The drums only flip forwards.
strings.mg.flap.hatch: Open maintenance hatch: the drums of the top line
strings.mg.flap.sheet.foot.1: ¹ Commission special for the conference, 12 to 14 February
strings.mg.flap.sheet.foot.2: ² Sundays and public holidays only
strings.mg.flap.sheet.foot.compact: ¹ Conference special, 12 to 14 February · ² Sundays and holidays only
strings.mg.flap.drum.title: Drum ‘{name}’ · {n} flaps
strings.mg.flap.notes.title: Alexei’s notes
strings.mg.flap.note.units_tens: At 9 → 0 the units carry the tens along.
strings.mg.flap.note.tens_hour: The tens carry the hour along.
strings.mg.flap.status.idle: One flap at a time. The train’s already here, after all.
strings.mg.flap.status.only_forward: Flaps only fall one way. The only way back is all the way round.
strings.mg.flap.status.drag: ‘{driven}’ turned too – that drum is linked to ‘{driver}’.
strings.mg.flap.status.carry: At 9 → 0 the units carried the tens along.
strings.mg.flap.fail.drag: ‘{driven}’ was already right and turned too – that drum is linked to ‘{driver}’.
strings.mg.flap.fail.carry: The tens were already right. On the jump from 9 to 0 the units carried them along.
strings.mg.flap.fail.probe: The motor rattles; the line doesn’t lock in. Different from the timetable: {fields}.
strings.mg.flap.fail.other_train: That’s how the timetable shows the train from {from} on platform {track}. Alexei’s train was the special on platform 5.
strings.mg.flap.solved: Clack. The line locks in: 8:41, MOSKVA via KARSK, platform 5. The KARSK flap is new – white, not yellowed.
strings.mg.flap.hint.1: Tip: Some drums carry a neighbour along when turned. Set the one that carries first – the one carried last.
strings.mg.flap.hint.2: Tip: First the units (at 9 → 0 the tens jump too), then the tens (they carry the hour), then the hour. On the right: first ‘from’ and ‘Platform’, ‘via’ last.
strings.explore.veltrava.hall.cloak_tokens.title: The cloakroom tokens
strings.explore.veltrava.hall.cloak_tokens.text: Herr Wenzel has been cloakroom attendant since 1927 and has never once mixed up a coat, he says. Today three delegations wanted out at once, and the hooks no longer matched. Pin, newspaper, scarf – everything could be assigned as on a clean plan. What remained was token 27: a dark grey woman’s coat with a burgundy scarf, and a burgundy cap above it. Fräulein Weiss handed it in today for the first time, says Herr Wenzel.
strings.mg.cloak.title: The cloakroom
strings.mg.cloak.subtitle: A break in the session. Everyone wants out at once, and in the rush Herr Wenzel has hung the coats on the wrong hooks.
strings.mg.cloak.instruction: Give every guest what is theirs. The numbers on the hooks are no longer right – pin, newspaper and scarf still are.
strings.mg.cloak.wenzel.name: Herr Wenzel
strings.mg.cloak.wenzel.start: The hooks are right, Herr Adler. Only the coats aren’t.
strings.mg.cloak.wenzel.hats: The hats! Ladies and gentlemen, the hats are still up on the shelf.
strings.mg.cloak.wenzel.end: That leaves two hats belonging to gentlemen still talking – and twenty-seven. Fräulein Weiss handed in her coat today for the first time.
strings.mg.cloak.status.taken: That has already been handed out.
strings.mg.cloak.hint.1: Tip: The number on the hook won’t help. Look at the pin on the lapel, the newspaper in the pocket and the scarf.
strings.mg.cloak.hint.2: Tip: The shape of the pin gives away the delegation – square, triangular, diamond, round. The newspaper gives away what someone reads.
strings.mg.cloak.hint.hats: Tip: Look at what the guest is wearing now. Pin, collar and scarf match the hat.
strings.mg.cloak.guest.imhof.name: Dr Imhof
strings.mg.cloak.guest.imhof.pin: On the lapel: the observers’ white diamond pin.
strings.mg.cloak.guest.imhof.wears: Now wearing the camel-hair coat and the green scarf.
strings.mg.cloak.guest.orlova.name: Frau Orlova
strings.mg.cloak.guest.orlova.pin: On the lapel: the Soviet delegation’s green triangle pin.
strings.mg.cloak.guest.orlova.wears: Now wearing the brown coat with the curly karakul collar.
strings.mg.cloak.guest.duval.name: Monsieur Duval
strings.mg.cloak.guest.duval.pin: On the lapel: the commission’s round pin.
strings.mg.cloak.guest.bauer.name: Herr Bauer
strings.mg.cloak.guest.bauer.pin: On the lapel: the Reich delegation’s square grey pin.
strings.mg.cloak.guest.bauer.wears: Now wearing the loden coat with the square pin.

strings.mg.cloak.coat.navy.desc: Navy coat · commission’s round pin · a dictionary in the pocket
strings.mg.cloak.coat.karakul.name: Coat with karakul collar
strings.mg.cloak.coat.karakul.desc: Dark brown coat · curly karakul collar · green triangle pin · a Moscow newspaper in the pocket
strings.mg.cloak.hat.ticket.name: Grey homburg
strings.mg.cloak.hat.ticket.desc: Grey homburg · a tram ticket in the band, route 7
strings.mg.cloak.hat.karakul.name: Karakul hat
strings.mg.cloak.hat.beret.name: Knitted cap
strings.mg.cloak.hat.pin.name: Grey homburg
strings.mg.cloak.hat.pin.desc: Grey homburg · square grey pin on the band
strings.mg.cloak.hat.ushanka.name: Fur hat
strings.mg.cloak.hat.ushanka.desc: Fur hat with ear flaps, smooth rabbit fur
strings.mg.cloak.hat.green.name: Black homburg
strings.mg.cloak.say.imhof.ask1: Imhof, token twelve. Camel hair, please – the Zurich paper is in the pocket. Nobody else here reads it.
strings.mg.cloak.say.imhof.thanks1: Merci vielmals. You would make a good observer, Herr Adler.
strings.mg.cloak.say.imhof.wrong1: I’m afraid not. Mine is camel hair.
strings.mg.cloak.say.imhof.hook12: Hook twelve, certainly – but that is loden. I wear camel hair.
strings.mg.cloak.say.imhof.elena: A woman’s coat? My wife would like that one. Mine is camel hair.
strings.mg.cloak.say.imhof.ask2: And my hat, please. The band is the colour of my scarf – my wife pays attention to such things.
strings.mg.cloak.say.imhof.thanks2: Merci. Now I look neutral again.
strings.mg.cloak.say.imhof.wrong2: No, no. Green like the scarf, please.
strings.mg.cloak.say.imhof.beret: A knitted cap? It doesn’t suit me, Herr Adler.
strings.mg.cloak.say.orlova.ask1: Orlova, thirty-one. Which one is mine? Surely you can see where I belong.
strings.mg.cloak.say.orlova.thanks1: Thank you. Back home there would be a form for this. In triplicate.
strings.mg.cloak.say.orlova.wrong1: No. Look at my pin, Herr Adler.
strings.mg.cloak.say.orlova.elena: That isn’t mine. It belongs to Fräulein Weiss; she translates for us.
strings.mg.cloak.say.orlova.ask2: And my hat. It matches the collar.
strings.mg.cloak.say.orlova.thanks2: Thank you. If the negotiations go like this, we’ll be done by Friday.
strings.mg.cloak.say.orlova.ushanka: Rabbit? That belongs to our driver.
strings.mg.cloak.say.orlova.beret: It’s very pretty. But not mine.
strings.mg.cloak.say.duval.ask1: Duval, booth one, token seven. Navy, with our round pin. A dictionary in the pocket – occupational hazard.
strings.mg.cloak.say.duval.thanks1: Merci. And the dictionary is still there too. A good day.
strings.mg.cloak.say.duval.elena: That belongs to Fräulein Weiss from booth two. Same pin, different coat.
strings.mg.cloak.say.bauer.ask1: Bauer, Reich Ministry of Transport, forty-four. The loden coat, please. Yesterday’s paper in the pocket.
strings.mg.cloak.say.bauer.thanks1: Thank you. I was already afraid I would have to report it.
strings.mg.cloak.say.bauer.wrong1: That is not mine. Loden, I said.
strings.mg.cloak.say.bauer.elena: A woman’s coat? Herr Adler, please.
strings.mg.cloak.say.bauer.ask2: Excuse me. My hat – the one that goes with the coat.
strings.mg.cloak.say.bauer.thanks2: Thank you. The Herr Ministerialdirektor does not like to be kept waiting.
strings.mg.cloak.say.bauer.wrong2: No. The one with our pin.
strings.mg.cloak.say.bauer.ticket: The tram? We have a car, Herr Adler.
